author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1968-10-11 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: Everyone will fight the good fight.
context_before: When I say “I” (or “my”) I mean “we,” for we are the gods who collectively form God. In the great play, God is fragmented and the one becomes the many. But before the state of Abraham we – in perfect unity – wrote the play for a divine purpose. We agreed to enter the world of death and completely forget who we are in order to make the play real. This we have done and we will return enhanced by the play, but we cannot stop half way or turn back, we must finish the race.
context_after: Everyone will go to the end and keep the faith we began in the state called Abraham.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from Before Abraham, Was I Am (1968-10-11).

quote_original: So, before Abraham, was I am.
context_before: eration, and your entrance denotes your position. There will be no menial parts there, for all will be a necessary part of the body of the Risen Lord.
context_after: That is God’s name forever and by this name he shall be known by all generations. God preceded his play, so the evangelist is telling the truth when he says, before Abraham, was I am.
